headline: Biology-informed representations sharpen protein and molecular property prediction
label: Biology Informed Protein Representation Learning
summary: Pretrained protein language models and surface or structure-aware encoders are being adapted with biological priors and confidence signals across tasks.
synthesis: The common thread is adaptation of pretrained representations, including protein language models, surface autoencoders, and affinity models, with explicit biological or structural priors. ProtDiS decomposes pretrained protein micro-environment embeddings into biologically grounded dimensions through an information-bottleneck objective. BERT-T6 fine-tunes ProtBert with imbalance-aware training to identify type VI secretion effectors, and a LoRA-adapted ESM-2 is evaluated for melting temperature prediction under cross-domain shift, with AUC 0.75-0.77. PSMa pretrains a masked autoencoder on protein molecular-surface point clouds for transfer to binding-site tasks, and ConfDTI uses AlphaFold2 pLDDT to modulate attention in drug-target interaction prediction. Benchmarking is a recurring element, with the Last Mile study comparing alchemical binding free energy and ML predictors on PDBbind and DUD-E. What is new is the injection of external biological priors, such as per-gene activity profiles in BioMADE and perception-consistency constraints in RAMS, into pretrained models.
